text.p: French shares slumped nearly two percent on Monday on concerns that interest rates were headed higher, brokers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 57.03 points, or 1.87 percent, at 2,992.41, and the CAC-40 August futures contract fell to 2,997 from 3,054.
"People are worried about the dollar's surge which will, sooner or later,force European central banks to react," a trader said.
He said some investors worry that the Bundesbank may nudge interest rates higher at its weekly money market operations on Tuesday.

But some market operators say the German central bank is unlikely to raise rates as such a gesture would probably not succeed in taming the dollar's advance to eight-year highs against the French and German currencies.
The latest U.S. data released on Friday showed strong growth, keeping alive worries of possible U.S. rate rises.
One trader said there was little on the horizon to suggest a fundamental reason for the dollar to pull back. Up to now, its advance had been viewed as a boon, notably for France's big export sector.
Traders said the selling on Monday did not worry them after the bourse's recent gains to all time highs. "We're around 3,000 points. That's not bad," one broker said.
The drop was exacerbated by Monday's lower than average volume of 7.14 billion francs, as many players in France are on holiday.
Valeo was the best performer on the CAC index, finishing up 2.34 percent after a favourable article on the car parts manufacturer in the weekly Journal des Finances.
Traders said the stock was catching up after lagging the rising car sector. They said Valeo also benefitted from the dollar's strength because of its considerable U.S. business.
The rest of the sector eased on profit-taking on Monday, notably carmaker Renault, whose stock closed down 3.53 percent.

Rhone-Poulenc's stock dropped 4.7 percent to 255.30 francs as some investors worried the dollar's strength and the U.S. market's recent gains would raise the price of its proposed buyout of minority shareholders in U.S.-based Rhone-Poulenc Rorer.
